question.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t-2⟩,$ use the cross product curvature formula to find the curvature of this curve as a function of $t.$ 

*Hint: You can use the fact that ${r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+4k.$*
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are told that

$$
{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+4k,
$$

we have

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{(\sqrt{5})^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
